Evidence is indirect: the located studies do not establish that better full-catalog training-target ranks or popularity-stratified training diagnostics predict held-out HR@10 gains specifically for NextItNet. [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) supports residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential prediction, without validating that diagnostic relationship. [Dong et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01801) explicitly distinguish memorization, generalization and subgroup performance. Crucially, [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled ranking metrics can reverse full-catalog model comparisons; full-catalog training ranks therefore cannot substitute for the pinned 99-negative validation HR@10.

Mechanistic evidence supports cautious hypotheses. [Denoising Implicit Feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04153) finds early high-loss interactions can indicate noise and demonstrates benefits from adaptive loss weighting; high loss alone does not establish noise in sparse items. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) demonstrates benefits from addressing false negatives in sequential recommendation, but uses a teacher, so its implementation should not be imported into this single-model experiment. [Schnabel et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05352) establish selection-bias problems; popularity counts alone cannot identify exposure propensities or genuine dislikes.

Proposed bounded protocol: freeze 200 training prefixes/category, stratified by training-only target frequency and history length; at three prespecified checkpoints, measure target-rank quantiles, positive–negative margins and loss, retaining targets while masking padding and applying a documented history-exclusion rule. Use strictly preceding inputs and final nonpadding readout. Compare these trajectories with unchanged validation HR@10 and subgroup counts. Improving training ranks with flat validation suggests testing regularization; weak margins suggest testing more negatives with observed-positive collision filtering. These are hypotheses requiring validation. Run one-factor ablations within budget, retain seed 42, and select solely by four-category macro validation HR@10. Each category retains one jointly trained NextItNet checkpoint; no auxiliary fitted scorer.
